wn.name: WaterCraft
wn.numbers: Everything here is a calculation aid. A water engineer checks every result; the numbers are not a certificate or a stamped design.
wn.privacy: Your network stays in this project and on this computer. Nothing is sent anywhere.
wn.stopped: Stopped early: the list is only what was done.
wn.more: {n} more rows are in the CSV.
wn.err.nonet: There is no water network in this project yet. Draw junctions, a reservoir and pipes with the Water mains tools first.
wn.err.noloads: Paste at least one load line first.
wn.err.trace_node: Pick the reservoir or tank the trace starts from.
wn.err.not_configured: WaterCraft could not reach the water solver. Reload the page.
wn.dem.help: One customer per line: id, x, y, kind, amount. Kind is one of {kinds}, or flow for a typed flow. Amount is units (homes), area (acres, or hectares in metric) or a flow. Each goes to the nearest junction.
wn.dem.share: Share a load between junctions within about 300 ft (90 m)
wn.pat.keep: Keep the pattern as it is
wn.dem.starting: The use per home or per acre is a starting value, not a standard. Replace it with your utility's own design figures before you trust a result.
wn.dem.result: {total} {u} in total on {n} junctions; {bad} lines could not be placed.
wn.dem.applied: Demands written to the water mains. Undo takes them back.
wn.fire.help: For each hydrant (or every junction when none is marked): the flow it can give while the pressure holds the residual, found with the same solver as the Water mains window.
wn.fire.mult: Demand multiplier (1 = the demand as drawn; use your peak-day factor)
wn.limit.system: the lowest point in the system
wn.crit.help: Takes each main out of service in turn and solves again: how much demand is cut off, and which junctions fall under the minimum pressure. With valves placed on the pipes you can take out a whole valved section.
wn.crit.segment: one valved section at a time
wn.crit.result: {n} outages tried; {cut} cut some customers off.
wn.q.help: Follows water through the 24-hour run: how old it is, how much chlorine is left, or where it came from. Uses the demand pattern and tank levels of the Water mains.
wn.q.result: {n} junctions outside the limits you set.
wn.q.limits: First-order decay only, a tank is one mixed volume, no booster stations yet. Run long enough for the pattern to repeat before you read the last day.
wn.pc.help: Reads the parcels drawn in this project. Each parcel becomes one customer at its centre; its use sets the demand. Say which parcel is which use, one per line as id = use (the ids and names are in the parcel list), or pick one use for the rest.
wn.pc.perunit: Area for one home (project area units; 0 = one home a parcel)
wn.pc.none: This project has no parcels yet. Draw or import them in CivilCraft first.
wn.pc.result: {n} parcels become customers, {total} {u} in all. {skipped} left out.
wn.sc.help: Each scenario is a name and changes to the network. Lines: close P12, open P12, demand x1.5, demand J5 120, diameter P3 16, c P4 80, pump P1 off, tank T1 level 130, reservoir R1 head 820, fire J9 1000. The first scenario is the base the others are compared with.
wn.sc.pdd: Let the pressure decide what is delivered (shortage run)
wn.sc.none: Write at least one scenario first.
wn.sc.lowest: The twelve junctions with the lowest pressure in any scenario:
wn.pd.help: An ordinary run delivers every demand whatever the pressure. Here a junction delivers only what its pressure allows: nothing at or under the lowest pressure, all of it at or over the full pressure. Add leaking joints (node, coefficient) and a leak along the pipes if you know them.
wn.pd.pmin: Pressure under which nothing is delivered ({p})
wn.pd.pref: Pressure at which all is delivered ({p})
wn.pd.emitters: Leaking joints: node, coefficient (flow per pressure^0.5)
wn.pd.leakc: Leak along pipes: flow per 1000 length units at 1 pressure unit (0 = none)
wn.pd.noconv: The iteration did not settle: read the numbers with care.
wn.pd.allserved: Every junction gets what it asks for.
wn.en.help: Control rules, one a line, in the usual words: LINK P1 CLOSED IF NODE T1 ABOVE 140, LINK P1 OPEN IF NODE T1 BELOW 110, LINK P1 OPEN AT TIME 6, LINK P1 CLOSED AT CLOCKTIME 22. Valves, one a line: id, pipe, FCV or PSV, setting (flow, or pressure). The run reports the tank levels, the rule events and what each pump costs to run.
wn.en.valves: Valves (id, pipe, FCV or PSV, setting in {q} or {p})
wn.en.patstep: Pattern step (seconds; blank = the project step)
wn.en.tariff: Price by hour of day (multipliers, 24 numbers; blank = flat)
wn.en.errors: These rule lines were not understood: {lines}.
wn.en.problems: {n} tank events (full or empty): the tank was held at its limit.
wn.em.help: What happens, and for how long, when something goes wrong. A main break takes the pipe out of service (the valves around it when valves are drawn); a fire draws water at a hydrant; a power cut stops the pumps (leave the pump box empty for all of them).
wn.em.pipe: Pipe (or pumps, for a power cut)
wn.em.result: Cut off at worst: {cut} {u} at {n} junctions. Lowest pressure {minp} {p}. First under the minimum: {first}.
wn.em.nolow: No junction falls under the minimum.
wn.cal.help: Readings from the field, one a line: pressure or flow, the junction or pipe, the value ({p} or {q}), and optionally the demand multiplier at the time. Groups of pipes whose roughness moves together, one a line: name: P1 P2 P3 (none = all pipes together). More readings than groups, please.
wn.cal.dm: Also fit one factor on every demand
wn.cal.result: Misfit before {a}, after {b} (1 means as close as the readings themselves are good to).
wn.cal.applied: The roughness is in the water mains; Undo puts it back.
wn.sz.help: Give the sizes you may buy ({d}, small to large, separated by commas) and a price per length unit for each (size = price, one a line). The run upsizes the pipes that help most for the money until every junction meets the pressure and no pipe is too fast, then takes back any size that was not needed. Pipes are never made smaller.
wn.sz.no: The sizes given cannot meet the limits ({n} pipes tried, {cost} in all). Add a larger size.
wn.sz.applied: The sizes are in the water mains; Undo puts them back.
wn.rh.help: Rehabilitation: old pipes carry a low roughness C. Name the options (name, new C, price per length unit, one a line) and a budget; the run picks the pipes that lift the pressures most per dollar. The minimum pressure and velocity above apply.
wn.rh.no: The budget or the options do not reach the limits: {n} pipes picked, {cost} spent.
